title: SAKE: Self-aware Knowledge Exploitation-Exploration for Grounded Multimodal Named Entity Recognition

problem.claim: Grounded Multimodal Named Entity Recognition must extract named entities and localize their visual regions in image-text pairs, but open-world social media settings contain long-tailed, rapidly evolving, and unseen entities.

gap.claim: External heuristic retrieval can introduce noisy or conflicting evidence, while relying only on internal MLLM knowledge is limited by knowledge boundaries and hallucination risk.

contributions.claim: SAKE is an end-to-end agentic framework that combines internal knowledge exploitation and external knowledge exploration through self-aware reasoning and adaptive search-tool invocation.
Difficulty-aware Search Tag Generation estimates entity-level uncertainty through multiple forward samplings to produce explicit knowledge-gap signals.
SAKE uses two-stage training with supervised fine-tuning on the SAKE-SeCoT dataset followed by agentic reinforcement learning with a hybrid reward that penalizes unnecessary retrieval.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on two widely used social media benchmarks.
The authors report that SAKE is effective on the two stated benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: GMNER extracts named entities and localizes their visual regions in image-text pairs.
Open-world social media introduces long-tailed, rapidly evolving, and unseen entities.
Existing methods use external retrieval or internal iterative refinement, but each has distinct precision, knowledge-boundary, or hallucination limitations.
SAKE combines self-aware reasoning and adaptive search with difficulty-aware signals, supervised tool-use training, and retrieval-penalizing agentic reinforcement learning.
The authors report experiments on two social media benchmarks and claim effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses uncertainty signals to decide when external retrieval is needed and penalizes unnecessary retrieval.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval may be most useful when model uncertainty indicates a knowledge gap rather than as a default operation.

application.claim: Systems combining internal generation with external tools could condition tool use on explicit uncertainty estimates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond GMNER or social media benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two benchmark names, dataset sizes, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or comparisons with baseline methods.
The abstract does not detail the hybrid reward, agentic reinforcement-learning procedure, or retrieval tools.
